name: Ephedrine

lead: Ephedrine is a stimulant from Ephedra plants, used medically to raise blood pressure during anesthesia. In looksmaxxing it is known as the ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin (ECA) stack, used for appetite suppression and energy during fasted cardio while cutting toward a leaner physique.

It stimulates adrenergic receptors and triggers norepinephrine release, which raises heart rate, blood pressure, alertness and energy expenditure and suppresses appetite. A 2003 JAMA meta-analysis examined it for weight loss and athletic performance, and a general reference summarises the findings as modest short-term weight loss, about 0.9 kg per month more than placebo. It is a milder thermogenic than clenbuterol or DNP.

paras: Guides on looksmax.org describe it as increasing energy and reducing hunger during a cut, typically as the ECA stack, with heart-health cautions attached. Forum users also pair it with MK-677 to offset hunger.

Reported effects include palpitations, fast heart rate, high blood pressure, restlessness and nausea, with more heart-related events than placebo in the meta-analysis. The FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements in 2004; the injectable is prescription-only.

angle.text: Ephedrine is the stimulant in the classic ECA stack, used to suppress appetite and lift energy for fasted cardio while cutting toward a leaner physique. It works by stimulating adrenergic receptors and releasing norepinephrine. Trials show modest fat loss, with raised heart rate and blood pressure.

lead: Ephedrine is a stimulant found naturally in Ephedra plants (ma huang) and also made synthetically; it raises alertness, heart rate and blood pressure and dampens appetite by prompting release of norepinephrine [1][2]. People who want a leaner, more defined physique have used it as a thermogenic and appetite suppressant: less body fat shows more muscle definition and a sharper facial and jaw outline, and fewer hunger pangs make a calorie deficit easier to keep. It is most often taken with caffeine, and sometimes aspirin, as the "ECA stack" [3][4][5].

Ephedrine has a long history. Ephedra-containing ma huang appears in Chinese medicine from the Han dynasty, the alkaloid was isolated in Japan in 1885, and Western medicine adopted it in the 1920s for asthma and congestion [2][1]. Today the injectable is a prescription drug used to prevent low blood pressure during anesthesia [6][2]. Ephedra weight-loss supplements were among the best-selling dietary supplements of the 1990s before the US Food and Drug Administration banned ephedrine-alkaloid supplements in April 2004, following reports of adverse events and the 2003 death of baseball pitcher Steve Bechler [7][8].

A 2003 JAMA meta-analysis found that ephedrine and ephedra produced modest short-term weight loss of roughly 0.6 to 1.0 kg per month more than placebo, with higher rates of palpitations and psychiatric, autonomic and gastrointestinal symptoms [9]. On looksmax.org it is discussed mainly for cutting phases, usually with heart-rate cautions [3][4].
infobox: Prohibited by WADA, IOC and major US leagues [7][2]

paras: Ephedrine is used by people cutting body fat, especially bodybuilders and physique-focused lifters, for three reasons they cite: appetite suppression, a mild rise in energy expenditure, and the energy to train hard while eating less [3][4]. Lower body fat is the appearance goal: visible abdominal and shoulder definition, and a leaner face with more prominent bone structure.

The ECA stack pairs ephedrine with caffeine and aspirin. A review of caffeine and ephedrine describes caffeine as having documented ergogenic effects, with ephedrine alone showing no significant performance gains and the pair often raising heart rate more than either alone [5]. The aspirin component is described by guide authors as extending the thermogenic action; no trial of that specific three-drug combination is cited here [3].
This use is not an approved indication, and in many countries the oral form is restricted or prescription-only [2].

The current US label for ephedrine sulfate injection lists treatment of clinically important hypotension in the setting of anesthesia [6]. Trials compare ephedrine with phenylephrine and norepinephrine during spinal anesthesia for caesarean delivery; a pooled analysis of seven randomised trials (292 women) found no difference in maternal hypotension between ephedrine and phenylephrine, with more maternal bradycardia on phenylephrine [10][11][12]. Neurology guidelines list ephedrine as a second-line option for orthostatic hypotension [13]. Historically it was used for asthma, nasal congestion, narcolepsy and obesity [2][1].

The 2003 JAMA meta-analysis searched nine databases and included unpublished and non-English work. No weight-loss trial lasted more than six months; pooled results showed modest loss of about 0.6 to 1.0 kg per month more than placebo depending on formulation, and no trial data on athletic performance with ephedra were found [9]. A general reference describes a 2021 systematic review reporting about 2 kg more loss than placebo over 4 to 24 weeks, with higher heart rate and changes in LDL and HDL cholesterol [2].

A dietetics review concluded that evidence for supplement weight-loss efficacy is inconclusive and that FDA alerts mean ephedra and ephedrine products cannot be recommended [14]. A 2012 laboratory study in ten healthy volunteers found that ephedrine raised blood pressure, heart rate and energy expenditure but, unlike cold exposure, did not activate brown adipose tissue [15].

Across 50 trials in the JAMA analysis, ephedrine or ephedra use was associated with 2.2- to 3.6-fold higher odds of psychiatric, autonomic or gastrointestinal symptoms and palpitations; the data could not assess events rarer than 1 in 1,000, and most case reports were poorly documented [9]. Common effects listed in general references include insomnia, anxiety, headache, raised blood pressure, fast heart rate and urinary retention, with stroke and heart attack among serious reports [2]. A case report describes a 22-year-old woman with cardiac ischemia changes after two days on an ephedrine-caffeine product [16]. A toxicology review places ephedrine among the naturally occurring amphetamine-type stimulants [17].

The injectable label lists nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, palpitations, reactive hypertension, bradycardia, dizziness and restlessness, warns about tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing, and cautions about severe hypertension with oxytocic drugs [6]. Ephedrine is contraindicated within 14 days of MAO inhibitors and with certain heart conditions, glaucoma and pheochromocytoma [2]. By 2004 the FDA had received over 18,000 adverse-event reports [2]. Guide authors on looksmax.org say the stack raises resting heart rate by at least 10 beats per minute, advise against high-intensity intervals while using it, and say it should not be used with heart problems [3][4].

Ephedrine directly stimulates alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors and indirectly causes release of norepinephrine from sympathetic nerve terminals; the label ascribes its pressor effect to increased arterial pressure, cardiac output and peripheral resistance [6]. In release assays it is mainly a norepinephrine releaser, with weak dopamine release and negligible serotonin release [2][18]. Comparative human studies from 1971 measured its effects against amphetamine, methamphetamine and methylphenidate [19].

Oral bioavailability is about 88 percent, onset is 15 to 60 minutes by mouth, effects last 2 to 4 hours orally, and the elimination half-life is about 6 hours; roughly 60 percent is excreted unchanged in urine, depending on urinary pH [2].

Ephedrine is a phenethylamine of formula C10H15NO with two chiral centres; the natural drug is the (1R,2S) form and pseudoephedrine is the (1R,2R) diastereomer [2][1]. It differs from methamphetamine by a hydroxyl group, which is why it is a controlled precursor under UN rules [2]. It occurs in more than 40 Ephedra species, but most medical ephedrine is now semi-synthetic [1][2].

Ma huang has been used in China for more than 2,000 years for asthma and bronchitis, and other Ephedra species were brewed by Native Americans and Mormon pioneers [7][2]. Nagayoshi Nagai isolated ephedrine in 1885 [1]. Keishi Chen and Carl Schmidt revived it for Western asthma treatment in the 1920s; Merck sold it as ephetonin, and exports from China to the West rose from 4 to 216 tonnes between 1926 and 1928 [1][2].

subs.h: Ephedra supplements and the US ban
paras: Through the 1990s ephedra weight-loss and energy products sold widely in the US. The FDA proposed limits in 1997 for products with 8 mg or more of ephedrine alkaloids; the top-selling brand Metabolife reported more than 14,000 adverse events and the proposal was withdrawn in 2000 after industry and congressional pushback [7]. In 2002 the Justice Department compelled Metabolife to hand over over 15,000 adverse-event reports [7]. Studies found labeled doses differing from measured content, sometimes tenfold between lots [7].

In February 2003 Baltimore Orioles pitcher Steve Bechler, 23, collapsed in spring training and died of multiple organ failure; the autopsy listed ephedra toxicity alongside a liver condition, mild hypertension, heat and low food intake [8]. Baseball's commissioner called for a ban and the FDA reopened its review [8]. The final rule banning ephedrine-alkaloid supplements was issued on April 12, 2004; ephedra extracts without ephedrine remain legal [7]. A Utah federal judge ruled against the FDA on low doses in April 2005, but the Tenth Circuit upheld the rule on August 17, 2006 and the Supreme Court declined review in 2007 [7][2].

In the United States ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements are banned and the injectable is prescription-only; traditional ma huang tea remains legal [2][7][6]. Pseudoephedrine sales are limited under the 2006 Combat Methamphetamine Epidemic Act [2]. Ephedrine is prescription-only in the UK, Australia and Germany (since April 2006), Schedule VI in Canada, and a precursor in Brazil [2]. A looksmax.org thread asks where members can find it, reflecting how national rules shape availability [20][3].

Ephedrine is prohibited by the IOC, WADA, the NCAA, MLB, NFL and PGA, with a urinary threshold of 10 micrograms per millilitre in WADA rules [2][7]. Footballer Diego Maradona (1994 World Cup) and several other athletes have tested positive [7]. A 2006 survey reported nearly half of collegiate hockey players had used ephedra [7].

On looksmax.org the ECA stack is promoted for appetite suppression, energy for cardio and mild thermogenesis, often described as weaker than clenbuterol or DNP [3][4]. A thread collects data on ephedrine and caffeine for preserving lean tissue during weight loss [21]. A 17-year-old poster asked about combining it with MK-677, and a reply raised whether a calorie deficit would hinder growth [22]. On T Nation, members mention ECA among fat-loss options, including with DNP [23][24][25].

The main weight-loss evidence is the 2003 JAMA meta-analysis of controlled trials [9], the 2004 review of caffeine and ephedrine in metabolism and performance [5], and the 2021 systematic review described in a general reference [2]. A mechanistic study found raised energy expenditure in healthy volunteers [15]. Registered anesthesia trials compare ephedrine with other vasopressors in caesarean delivery [11][12][10]. A randomised trial in myasthenia gravis and a trial on hemostatic effects address other conditions [26][27].

lore.intro: Ephedrine appears on looksmax.org mainly through the ECA stack, presented as an appetite-suppressing, energising aid for cutting, with frequent heart-safety disclaimers; T Nation members mention it among fat-loss options [3][4][23].

claims.claim: The ECA stack kills appetite and gives energy for fasted cardio while preserving lean tissue.
ECA is a mild thermogenic, much weaker than clenbuterol, albuterol or DNP.
It is acceptable if you have no heart problems and track heart rate, and exercise should be low-intensity.
Adding caffeine makes ephedrine work much better.
Ephedrine can be stacked with MK-677 to counter hunger while building muscle and height.
The FDA ban on ephedra supplements was not justified at low doses.
Ephedrine preserves muscle during a cut.
